text:
Marta: FYI onprem admin team can't access private control plane after the RBAC refactor deploy about 10m ago :warning:
Raj: ack, are they getting 403s or connection errors?
Marta: 403s when hitting /admin/ui and when trying `kubectl` against the onprem cluster gateway. One report: `rpc: permission denied`
Amanda: :eyes: I'm seeing related alerts from the control plane: several `AccessDenied` entries to KMS key `redwood-onprem-master` at 2024-11-03T14:22:11Z
Auditbot: audit-log: user=marta action=admin.ui access=denied reason=missing_binding resource=private-controlplane at 2024-11-03T14:22:12Z
Raj: that sounds like the RBAC change removed a clusterrolebinding that included the KMS service account. I pulled the migration diff: the `priv-admins` role was narrowed and we unintentionally removed `system:kms:wrap` from the onprem binding.
Chris: timeline? which PR?
Raj: PR 7293 merged 14:10 UTC. I can revert the role narrowing but want a short mitigation first.
Marta: customers on dedicated/private are blocked for admin ops; need fast mitigation.
Amanda: quick workaround: re-add a temporary binding that includes the KMS role for the onprem service account and allowlist the ci-ops IP in VPC so ops can reach the control plane.
Chris: can someone run this? `kubectl create clusterrolebinding tmp-priv-kms --clusterrole=priv-admins --user=svc-kms@onprem` — but verify the subject name first.
Raj: don't create a long-lived binding. I'll create a temp binding with TTL via our infra job and also trigger a policy patch:
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: tmp-onprem-kms-access
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: svc-kms
  namespace: redwood-system
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: priv-admins
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```
Marta: doing it now. Patch applied at 14:30 UTC.
Sre-bot: deploy-bot: clusterrolebinding/tmp-onprem-kms-access created by marta at 2024-11-03T14:30:42Z
Amanda: after binding, a few admins report they can access the console again.
Auditbot: audit-log: user=svc-kms action=decrypt access=allowed key=redwood-onprem-master at 2024-11-03T14:31:12Z
Raj: good. Next: add an automated test in CI to catch missing KMS-related bindings when RBAC changes land, and add a pre-merge policy check that flags removals of `system:kms:*` mappings for private control planes.
Chris: also there's a secondary issue: the VPC allowlist denied fallback when the control plane scaled and routed traffic to the new HA endpoint. We should have had a permissive internal fallback for admin ops during role transitions.
Marta: logged an infra ticket: INFRA-1834 to add ephemeral allowlist fallback and to improve runbook.
Raj: I'll open a security PR to revert the narrowing change and then a follow-up that reintroduces the narrowed role but preserves KMS bindings and includes integration tests.
Amanda: +1. Also schedule an audit entry to track who merged RBAC deltas without the checklist.
Chris: can we add a lint rule to the rbac-linter to warn when a change removes subjects bound to resources named `kms` or `key`?
Raj: yes, I'll prototype a linter rule.
Marta: thanks everyone. Postmortem? short blameless one: describe root cause (RBAC refactor removed KMS binding), impact (admin ops blocked), mitigation (temp binding + VPC allowlist), fix (revert + tests + linter), owners: raj/amanda/marta.
Sre-bot: incident ticket created: SEC-6623 (severity: high, owner: raj)
Amanda: I'll draft the postmortem and ping legal for any compliance notices for affected customers.
Chris: one follow-up: run a scan across dedicated/private clusters to confirm no other roles lost KMS access during the refactor. Raj?
Raj: on it, running `rbac-diff` across all control planes now, will post results in this thread.
Marta: thanks. keep updates here only.
